# A transaction and a split each naming a custom key empty.
#
# `key: ""` clears, and removing a custom key is what clearing one means —
# the rule README states under "What a key says, and what leaving it out
# says", which holds for reserved fields and custom metadata alike, on every
# block.
#
# Read only as "not None", an empty value was stored as an empty key on a
# transaction the book did not yet have. The export then wrote `department: ""`
# back, so the file grew a line nobody typed; and because the same file
# imported into a book that already held the transaction removes the key
# instead, the same ledger produced two different books depending on which
# book it met. A create → export → re-import cycle did not settle.
#
# Owners, invoices and bills have never had this: they merge through one
# function that pops an empty value on both paths.
#
# What this fixture produces: one transaction carrying `region: "west"` and
# `department: ""`, whose bank split carries `project: ""`.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_an_empty_key_is_not_stored_empty.py.
2026-01-01 commodity CAD
	mnemonic: "CAD"
	fullname: "Canadian Dollar"
	namespace: "CURRENCY"
	fraction: 100
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Sundry
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-02-01 * "Kept some keys, cleared others"
	region: "west"
	department: ""
	Assets:Bank -20.00 CAD
		project: ""
	Expenses:Sundry 20.00 CAD
